LanguageData.POK.Tut.P1.Title: 1. Heads-up hold'em
LanguageData.POK.Tut.P1.Body:
Two players. Each of you gets **two cards only you can see**, and **five shared cards** come down in the middle of the table.

The best five-card hand out of those seven takes the pot. You do not have to use both of your own cards.

Take all of their chips and you win. If nobody is broke after twenty-four hands, the bigger stack wins.
LanguageData.POK.Tut.P2.Title: 2. How a hand unfolds
LanguageData.POK.Tut.P2.Body:
Every hand starts with forced bets — the blinds. Whoever has the dealer button posts the smaller one and acts **first**.

There is a round of betting on your two cards, another after three shared cards (the flop), another on the fourth (the turn), and a last one on the fifth (the river).

The blinds double every eight hands. That is what makes the game end.
LanguageData.POK.Tut.P3.Title: 3. What to do on your turn
LanguageData.POK.Tut.P3.Body:
With nothing to match you **check**. If they have bet, you **call** it or **fold**. To put in more, you **raise**.

There is one thing worth remembering — compare what the call costs against what the pot is paying you. If the pot holds 100 and the call is 20, winning one time in five breaks even.

You cannot bet more than the other player can cover, which is why there are no side pots here.
LanguageData.POK.Tut.P4.Title: 4. What beats what
LanguageData.POK.Tut.P4.Body:
Weakest first: high card, a pair, two pair, three of a kind, a straight, a flush, a full house, four of a kind, a straight flush.

Within a rank the higher cards win, and if those tie the leftover cards (the kickers) decide it. Suits never break a tie.

An unfinished game stays on the table. The cards are not saved — the deal comes from a seed — so closing the window brings back the very same hand.
